statement: Define the clockwise 90-degree rotation R(A) of an n x n matrix A by R(A)[i][j] = A[n-1-j][i] for 0 <= i,j < n, and set R^0(A)=A, R^1(A)=R(A), R^2(A)=R(R(A)), R^3(A)=R(R(R(A))). Whenever find_rotation(mat, target) returns a Bool r, r = true if and only if there exists k in {0,1,2,3} such that target[i][j] = R^k(mat)[i][j] for every 0 <= i,j < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(mat). Assume 1 <= n <= 10, len(target) = n, len(mat[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, len(target[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, and mat[i][j] and target[i][j] are each either 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, find_rotation(mat, target) returns a result r (a Bool); it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access any index outside 0 <= i,j < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(mat). Assume 1 <= n <= 10, len(target) = n, len(mat[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, len(target[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, and mat[i][j] and target[i][j] are each either 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Define R(A)[i][j] = A[n-1-j][i] for 0 <= i,j < n. Let mat' be the n x n matrix with mat'[i][j] = R(mat)[i][j] for every 0 <= i,j < n. Whenever find_rotation(mat, target) returns r1 and find_rotation(mat', target) returns r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: Let n = len(mat). Assume 1 <= n <= 10, len(target) = n, len(mat[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, len(target[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, and mat[i][j] and target[i][j] are each either 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Define R(A)[i][j] = A[n-1-j][i] for 0 <= i,j < n. Let target' be the n x n matrix with target'[i][j] = R(target)[i][j] for every 0 <= i,j < n. Whenever find_rotation(mat, target) returns r1 and find_rotation(mat, target') returns r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: Let n = len(mat). Assume 1 <= n <= 10, len(target) = n, len(mat[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, len(target[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, and mat[i][j] and target[i][j] are each either 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Define transpose T(A) by T(A)[i][j] = A[j][i] for 0 <= i,j < n. Whenever find_rotation(mat, target) returns r1 and find_rotation(T(mat), T(target)) returns r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: Let n = len(mat). Assume 1 <= n <= 10, len(target) = n, len(mat[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, len(target[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, and mat[i][j] and target[i][j] are each either 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever find_rotation(mat, target) returns a Bool r with r = true, the number of entries equal to 1 in mat equals the number of entries equal to 1 in target; that is, sum over 0 <= i,j < n of mat[i][j] equals sum over 0 <= i,j < n of target[i][j].
preconditions: Let n = len(mat). Assume 1 <= n <= 10, len(target) = n, len(mat[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, len(target[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, and mat[i][j] and target[i][j] are each either 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n.
